units.title: Gender
units.intro: Grammar: the past tenses (simple, continuous, perfect) and how they work together in sentences with when, while, before and after.

cards.title: Past tenses (review)
rule: **Past simple** (verb + -ed or irregular form) = a finished action at a past time: *She **won** the race in 2019.*
**Past continuous** (was/were + -ing) = an action in progress at a past moment: *At 8 pm they **were studying**.*
**Past perfect** (had + past participle) = an action that happened **before** another past action: *The film **had started** when we arrived.*

examples.text: I visited my aunt last week.
I was visit my aunt last week.
examples.fix: I visited my aunt last week.

examples.text: When I arrived, the meeting had already begun.
She has finished the work yesterday.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and ________ after reviewing our academic portfolios.

steps.text: The pronoun follows the preposition 'to' and forms part of a compound prepositional object ('to Aster and [pronoun]').
This slot requires the objective case ($$\text{Preposition} + \text{Object Pronoun}$$).
Students often write 'Aster and I' because 'Aster and I' is common in the subject position.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still functional, but ________ keys are difficult to press.

steps.text: The blank modifies the noun 'keys' to show ownership.
Students often confuse 'its' (possessive adjective) with 'it's' (contraction of 'it is' or 'it has').

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The candidate ________ the board selected for the position has outstanding credentials.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The relative pronoun refers to 'The candidate' (a person). The clause that follows has a subject-verb pattern: 'the board' (Subject) + 'selected' (Verb). This indicates the relative pronoun is acting as the object of 'selected'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
While 'who' is increasingly used as an object pronoun in casual speech, formal academic exams strictly enforce 'whom' for objective relative slots ($$\text{Whom} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ን 'The candidate' (ሰብ) ክውክል ከሎ፡ ድሕሪኡ ዘሎ ሓረግ 'the board selected' (Subject + Verb) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ኣብ ቦታ ተቐባሊ (object) እዩ ዘሎ። ስለዚ ኣብ ስሩዕ ሰዋስው 'whom' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። 'Who' ኣብ ናይ ዋና ባእታ (subject) ቦታ ጥራይ እዩ ዝስራዕ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Since both Almaz and her sister wanted to complete the project quickly, they did all the research ________.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject is 'they' (plural). The corresponding plural reflexive pronoun is 'themselves' ($$\text{They} \rightarrow \text{themselves}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Options A ('theirselves') and D ('by theirselves') are non-standard forms. Tigrinya speakers often use 'theirselves' because they translate 'ባዕላቶም' directly based on the possessive modifier 'their'.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ናይ 'they' (ንሳቶም) ነብሰ-ኣንጸባራቒ ተውላጠ ስም (reflexive pronoun) 'themselves' (Option B - ባዕላቶም) እዩ። 'Theirselves' ዝብል ቃል ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ሰዋስው ፈጺሙ የለን፤ እዚ ልሙድ ናይ ተማሃሮ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Past tenses in adverbial clauses
rule: **Past continuous + past simple:** a longer action interrupted by a short one: *While she **was cooking**, the phone **rang**.*
**Past perfect + past simple:** the earlier action uses the past perfect: *After he **had finished** his homework, he **went** out.*
Use **while** with the longer (continuous) action and **when** usually with the short action.

examples.text: While we were walking home, it started to rain.
While we walked home, it was starting to rain.
examples.fix: While we were walking home, it started to rain.

examples.text: Before the teacher came, we had cleaned the class.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "While we walked home, it was starting to rain."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** **Past continuous + past simple:** a longer action interrupted by a short one: *While she **was cooking**, the phone **rang**.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "While we walked home, it was starting to rain." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "While we were walking home, it started to rain."
**Check:** **Past perfect + past simple:** the earlier action uses the past perfect: *After he **had finished** his homework, he **went** out.*

cards.answer: While we were walking home, it started to rain.

cards.title: Common mistakes
head: Wrong
Right
Why
rows: After did, use the base form.
Know is a state verb: no -ing.
Use the past participle after had.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Picture a timeline: **had done** is further back than **did**; **was doing** is the long line, **did** is the short dot that cuts it.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Past simple = finished past action; past continuous = action in progress; past perfect = earlier past action. While + continuous for the long action, when + simple for the short one; the earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Sham ________ her schedule repeatedly before the event started.
cards.why: The sentence describes an action that happened before another action in the past ('before the event started'). This requires the Past Perfect tense (had + V3).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: When I was waiting for the bus at the bus stop, the man next to me _________ chatting.
cards.why: The sentence describes an action that interrupted or happened during another past action. The interruption is expressed in the **Simple Past** ('started').

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: When the teacher reached the staff, she found the director ____ out.
cards.why: The Past Perfect ('had just gone') is used for an action that was completed before another action in the past ('reached').

glossary.meaning: The third form of a verb: gone, written, played.
A clause beginning with when, while, after, before, etc., telling when something happened.

tips.text: Picture a timeline: **had done** is further back than **did**; **was doing** is the long line, **did** is the short dot that cuts it.

games.title: Match the form to its example

questions.q: When I got to the station, the train ____.
questions.label: 1. When I got to the station, the train ____.

similar.q: Choose: When the bell rang, the students (ran / were running) out.
similar.a: ran. The bell rang and then they ran: two short actions in sequence use the past simple.

similar.q: Correct the error: He had saw the film before.
similar.a: He had seen the film before. After had, use the past participle seen.

why: Answer B: had already left
Two past actions: getting to the station and the train leaving.
The train left first, so use the past perfect: had already left.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: While she ____ the floor, she found a ring.
questions.label: 2. While she ____ the floor, she found a ring.

similar.q: Correct the error: He had saw the film before.
similar.a: He had seen the film before. After had, use the past participle seen.

similar.q: Join with after: She finished her exam. She went home.
similar.a: After she had finished her exam, she went home. The earlier action takes the past perfect.

why: Answer C: was sweeping
While shows the longer action in progress.
Use the past continuous: was sweeping.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.label: 3. They ____ to Massawa last summer.

similar.q: Join with after: She finished her exam. She went home.
similar.a: After she had finished her exam, she went home. The earlier action takes the past perfect.

similar.q: Choose: I (was reading / read) when you called.
similar.a: was reading. Reading was in progress when the short action (you called) happened.

why: Answer B: went
Last summer is a finished past time.
Use the past simple: went.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.label: 4. ____ you see the match yesterday?

similar.q: Choose: I (was reading / read) when you called.
similar.a: was reading. Reading was in progress when the short action (you called) happened.

similar.q: Choose: When the bell rang, the students (ran / were running) out.
similar.a: ran. The bell rang and then they ran: two short actions in sequence use the past simple.

why: Answer B: Did
Past simple question with a main verb: Did + subject + base verb.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: At nine o’clock last night, we ____ television.
questions.label: 5. At nine o’clock last night, we ____ television.

similar.q: Choose: When the bell rang, the students (ran / were running) out.
similar.a: ran. The bell rang and then they ran: two short actions in sequence use the past simple.

why: Answer B: were watching
A point in past time with an action in progress.
Past continuous: were watching.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: After the guests ____ (leave), we washed the dishes.
questions.label: 6. After the guests ____ (leave), we washed the dishes.

similar.q: Correct the error: He had saw the film before.
similar.a: He had seen the film before. After had, use the past participle seen.

why: Leaving happened before washing.
Earlier past action: past perfect had + left.
questions.tip: Say the sentence aloud with your answer; it must be grammatical and make sense.

questions.q: I ____ (not / understand) the question, so I asked the teacher.
questions.label: 7. I ____ (not / understand) the question, so I asked the teach

similar.q: Join with after: She finished her exam. She went home.
similar.a: After she had finished her exam, she went home. The earlier action takes the past perfect.

why: Understand is a state verb, so no continuous form.
Past simple negative: did not + base verb.
questions.tip: Say the sentence aloud with your answer; it must be grammatical and make sense.

questions.q: The lights went out while we ____ (have) dinner.
questions.label: 8. The lights went out while we ____ (have) dinner.

similar.q: Choose: I (was reading / read) when you called.
similar.a: was reading. Reading was in progress when the short action (you called) happened.

why: Dinner was in progress when the lights went out.
Past continuous with we: were having.
questions.tip: Say the sentence aloud with your answer; it must be grammatical and make sense.

questions.label: 9. She ____ (write) three letters before breakfast.

similar.q: Choose: When the bell rang, the students (ran / were running) out.
similar.a: ran. The bell rang and then they ran: two short actions in sequence use the past simple.

why: Before breakfast refers to an earlier past time than the story.
Past perfect: had + written (past participle of write).
questions.tip: Say the sentence aloud with your answer; it must be grammatical and make sense.
